definition: One of the discrete energies that an electron bound in an atom is allowed to have. The lowest is the ground state; the higher ones are excited states.

A change of an electron from one energy level of an atom to another. Moving down emits one photon whose energy equals the gap; moving up needs exactly that energy, for example from an absorbed photon.
A single packet, or quantum, of electromagnetic radiation. A photon of frequency $f$ carries energy $E = hf$.
The constant $h$ that links a photon's energy to its frequency in $E = hf$; $h = \pu{6.63e-34 J s}$, given in the data booklet.
A continuous spectrum crossed by dark lines, formed when light passes through a cooler gas whose atoms absorb photons of particular wavelengths.

One particular wavelength emitted or absorbed by atoms, seen as a bright line in an emission spectrum or a dark line in an absorption spectrum. Each line comes from a transition between two energy levels.
